title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
authors: Kentaro Nakajo, Hojun Im, Keiichiro Nishimura, Masahiro Teraoka, Masaya Kikuchi
abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved photovoltaic efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against ambient degradation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, environmentally stable hybrid Schottky solar cells on untextured silicon.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer devices against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier.
infographic.evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 ambient-exposure days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
infographic.watch_item: The reported 75-day ambient test does not establish long-term outdoor durability or manufacturing-scale barrier integrity.
infographic.paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells

title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
authors: Shafi Bin Sultan, Sabik Bin Sultan, Mohammad Tajrian Arafat Alvi, Rayhanul Islam Sony, Abdulah Al Numan
abstract: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. The proposed model leverages TFT to learn short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance, while N-BEATS captures long-term trend and seasonal components through interpretable basis decomposition. An adaptive attention mechanism dynamically fuses both branches, enabling balanced multi-scale learning. The framework simultaneously generates forecasts for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour horizons within a single unified pipeline. The model is evaluated using multi-year real-world datasets from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11 across the 20162017, 2023, 2024, and 20252026 datasets, respectively, corresponding to a 3540% reduction compared to the best baseline (TFT). Additionally, MAPE remains below 5% across all datasets, indicating high predictive accuracy and stability. The model also provides interpretability through attention visualization and trendseasonality decomposition, and is deployed on a cloud-based platform for real-time forecasting. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is robust, interpretable, and suitable for practical renewable energy applications.

infographic.key_insight: A hybrid TFT–N-BEATS model combines short-term dynamics with long-term patterns to improve multi-horizon photovoltaic power forecasting.
infographic.engineering_relevance: More accurate PV forecasts can support grid stability, energy scheduling, and coordinated PV–battery–grid operation.
method: TFT learns short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes long-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches to forecast 30 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours, 12 hours, and 24 hours ahead.

infographic.watch_item: RMSE units and horizon-specific results are not provided in the abstract; the work addresses PV forecasting rather than perovskite cell materials or device performance.
infographic.paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Sofiia Kosar, Anil R. Pininti, Vladyslav Hnapovskyi, José P. Jurado, Subhashri Mannar, Lorenzo Mardegan
abstract: The scalable fabrication of high-quality, large-area perovskite thin films is hindered by microscopic inhomogeneities, particularly residual compositional impurities formed during processing. Identifying these impurities, understanding their impact on device operation, and enabling their rapid detection are essential for upscaling perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, nano-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy combined with high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques was used to identify detrimental impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films relevant to tandem solar cells. Photo-stress experiments revealed that degradation of the perovskite layer initiates at impurity-perovskite interfaces, demonstrating that impurities act as failure nucleation sites. Leveraging these insights, a rapid, non-invasive, and high-throughput framework based on high-resolution reflected light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis was developed, enabling detection and quantification of harmful impurities in as-prepared films within seconds. Films with higher impurity density show accelerated early degradation, establishing this parameter as an early-warning metric for stability screening. Extending this framework to degradation tracking further reveals coupled photo- and thermo-chemical contributions to impurity-mediated instability. Overall, this work establishes a practical chemically-validated diagnostic imaging framework for rapid pre-screening of perovskite films to enable stable and scalable PSCs.

infographic.key_insight: Microscopic impurities act as degradation nucleation sites in wide-bandgap perovskite films, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can flag them within seconds.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could help prioritize stable perovskite films for scalable tandem solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation onset.
Detect and quantify impurities with reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
infographic.evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation initiating at impurity–perovskite interfaces, while films with higher impurity density exhibited faster early degradation.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not report detection accuracy or validate impurity density as a predictor of long-term device lifetime.
infographic.paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells

title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou, Gaoxiang Yuan
abstract: While retrieval-augmented language models increasingly serve as literature assistants in the physical sciences, existing benchmarks evaluate them primarily on qualitative text overlap or through model-based scoring rather than against verified experimental ground truth. In experimental materials disciplines such as perovskite photovoltaics, however, the most critical inquiries are inherently quantitative and aggregate measurements across dozens or hundreds of papers. Here, we present a quantitative question-answering benchmark where all 755 ground-truth answers are computed directly from 45,441 measured device records (40,889 human-curated records through 2021 and 4,552 records extracted from 2022-2026 literature). Benchmarking six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers using an open 14B model on a single 24 GB GPU, standard passage retrieval tops out at 16-23% accuracy (compared to 1.6-6.5% zero-shot). In contrast, equipping the language model with read-only SQL execution over the structured device table elevates accuracy to 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature -- a 33.01.8 percentage-point advantage over hybrid text retrieval. Aggregate queries spanning extrema, distributions, and filtered record counts prove virtually unsolvable via text retrieval alone, demonstrating that systematic table extraction is an operational prerequisite for literature-scale quantitative inquiry.

infographic.key_insight: Read-only SQL access to structured perovskite device data raises quantitative question-answering accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% with standard passage retrieval.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reliable literature-scale comparisons of perovskite solar cells require structured experimental records, not text retrieval alone.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers directly from 45,441 measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures across 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers.
Equip an open 14B model with read-only SQL access on a single 24 GB GPU.
infographic.evidence_signal: SQL-enabled accuracy reached 51.5% on historical literature and 50.8% on prospective literature, while zero-shot accuracy was 1.6–6.5%.
infographic.watch_item: Accuracy remains near 51%, and deployment depends on accurate extraction and maintenance of structured device records.
infographic.paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics

title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou
abstract: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. To solve this, we mapped the institutional provenance of the Perovskite Database and established a rigorous hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications, and institutions. Benchmarking thirteen models establishes new state-of-the-art performance across all splits and reveals a critical regime shift: while tree ensembles dominate random splits by recognising familiar recipes, their ranking collapses on genuinely unseen institutions and future discoveries, where composition-aware neural architectures excel. Furthermore, feature importance demonstrates that the device architecture and fabrication methodology dictate final efficiency just as strongly as the absorber chemistry. This standardised protocol empowers the community to separate memorisation from true physical discovery.

infographic.key_insight: Random data splits can reward memorisation of duplicated perovskite solar-cell recipes rather than generalisation to new institutions and future discoveries.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Provenance-grouped evaluation can help engineers select models for genuinely new device designs while accounting for chemistry, architecture and fabrication.
method: Map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Use hierarchical grouped splits to isolate duplicate devices, publications and institutions.
Benchmark 13 models and analyse feature importance.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another; tree ensembles lead on random splits, while composition-aware neural architectures excel on unseen institutions and future discoveries.
infographic.watch_item: Reliable grouped evaluation depends on accurate provenance metadata and consistent identification of duplicate recipes.
infographic.paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics

title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
authors: Dayin Chen, Xiaodan Shi, Xin Xu, Zhongyue Su, Shibo Zhu, Ruizhe Deng
abstract: The rapid growth of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation is increasing the demand for accurate forecasting across large numbers of geographically dispersed stations. Existing approaches are commonly developed for individual sites or specific forecasting horizons, requiring repeated training and maintenance as new stations are integrated and limiting direct reuse at previously unseen sites. To address this scalability gap, this paper presents a domain-specific foundation-style pretraining framework that learns a shared forecasting model from heterogeneous multi-site and multi-horizon PV data. NWP-assisted forecasting is formulated as a sequence-completion problem that unifies historical PV power, meteorological observations, future numerical weather prediction (NWP) forecasts, and time encodings. Three pretraining objectives are designed and systematically evaluated, including forecast-aligned reconstruction, generic reconstruction, and mixed reconstruction. The mixed objective combines the operational structure of PV forecasting with random sequence reconstruction and provides the most balanced performance across forecasting accuracy, degraded NWP conditions, and downstream adaptation. Experiments on 479 distributed PV stations use 340 stations for model development and 139 spatially held-out stations for zero-shot evaluation. Across horizons from 6 hours to 7 days, the multi-site pretrained MR model outperforms representative station-specific and shared baselines, as well as generalist time-series models, including a recent large-scale pretrained foundation model. The pretrained model can also be directly deployed at new PV stations and subsequently adapted to region-specific operational objectives when local data become available, providing a scalable forecasting paradigm for large distributed PV fleets.

infographic.key_insight: A shared, domain-pretrained model forecasts distributed PV generation across sites and horizons, including previously unseen stations without local retraining.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Fleet-wide forecasting could reduce per-station model training and maintenance while supporting later adaptation to local operating needs.
method: Frame forecasting as sequence completion using historical PV power, weather observations, future NWP forecasts, and time encodings.
Pretrain across heterogeneous sites and forecasting horizons.
Compare forecast-aligned, generic, and mixed reconstruction objectives; mixed reconstruction provides the most balanced performance.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation spans 479 PV stations—340 for development and 139 spatially held out for zero-shot testing—with reported gains over station-specific, shared, and generalist baselines across 6-hour to 7-day horizons.
infographic.watch_item: Deployment still requires validating NWP quality and transfer performance under weather and site conditions beyond the evaluated fleet.
infographic.paper_title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting

title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Rustam Arabov, Konstantin Sozykin, Nikita Rybin, Alexander Shapeev
abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

infographic.key_insight: Symmetry-based low-rank fine-tuning enables one MatterSim 1M potential to predict lattice thermal conductivity across compounds sharing a crystal symmetry, including compounds not used in fine-tuning.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Faster thermal-conductivity screening could support thermal management and materials selection for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications.
method: Select a small set of compounds sharing a crystal symmetry.
Fine-tune MatterSim 1M using symmetry-based few-shot low-rank adaptation.
Calculate lattice thermal conductivity by solving the Boltzmann transport equation.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across half-Heuslers (space group 216), space-group-225 materials, and spinels (227), mean absolute relative differences from moment tensor potential and polyMLP references were 2–3× smaller than for untuned MatterSim 1M; potential preparation for 100 compounds was approximately 5–7× faster than individual fine-tuning.
infographic.watch_item: Transfer is demonstrated within shared-symmetry material groups, not across arbitrary crystal structures, and the abstract reports no direct solar-cell device validation.
infographic.paper_title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity

title: Climate-Driven Supply-Demand Matching Reshapes Global SolarEV Decarbonization Potential
authors: Yuchen Liu, Stefan Pfenninger-Lee, Tosiyuki Nakaegawa, Takuro Kobashi
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaics (PV) can support rapid urban decarbonization, but their contribution is constrained by the imbalance between PV generation and demand, both shaped by local climate. Growing urban electric-vehicle (EV) deployment creates distributed storage near rooftop PV, shifting PV electricity across time. Here we simulate rooftop PV integrated with EVs as batteries across 5,000 grid cells globally, using hourly meteorology and climate-induced demand. We find that PV-EV systems can supply up to 84% of annual building and mobility electricity demand. Self-sufficiency is highest where daytime demand aligns with generation and seasonal variability remains limited. Using PV capacity factor alone to screen PV-EV potential undervalues 21.9% of the world's 1,000 most populous cities because generation-side metrics overlook the temporal coupling of PV generation, electricity demand and EV storage. Substantial PV-EV potential is concentrated in many low-latitude cities, offering a pathway to cleaner urban energy systems while accelerating progress towards carbon neutrality.

infographic.key_insight: Matching rooftop solar generation with climate-driven demand and EV battery storage can supply up to 84% of annual building and mobility electricity needs.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Urban PV-EV planning should prioritize hourly supply-demand alignment and seasonal variability, rather than solar capacity factor alone.
method: Simulate rooftop PV coupled with EV batteries across 5,000 global grid cells.
Use hourly meteorology and climate-induced electricity demand.
Assess self-sufficiency and compare potential with capacity-factor-based screening.
infographic.evidence_signal: The simulations indicate that capacity-factor-only screening undervalues PV-EV potential in 21.9% of the world's 1,000 most populous cities.
infographic.watch_item: Real-world performance will depend on EV availability for storage and charging coordination; the reported potential is simulation-based.
infographic.paper_title: Climate-Driven Supply-Demand Matching Reshapes Global SolarEV Decarbonization Potential

title: Learning Inter-Graph Interactions Between Heterogeneous Substructures of Chemical Systems
authors: Gyoung S. Na
abstract: Complex chemical systems containing heterogeneous substructures are common in real-world applications. Various physical phenomena of the complex chemical systems are derived from the interactions between the heterogeneous substructures. However, existing graph representation learning methods for inter-graph interactions assumed graph-level interactions between homogeneous structures, such as organic molecules and inorganic crystalline materials. We propose a data descriptor of the complex chemical systems and a graph neural network for learning inter-graph interactions between organic and inorganic compounds. We applied the proposed method to predict the physical properties of hybrid solar cell materials containing heterogeneous substructures, which have received significant attention for sustainable energy resources. By learning heterogeneous inter-graph interactions, the proposed method achieved state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting band gaps of 1,682 hybrid solar cell materials.

infographic.key_insight: Learning interactions between organic and inorganic substructures improves band-gap prediction for hybrid solar cell materials.
infographic.engineering_relevance: More accurate band-gap predictions could support computational screening of hybrid materials for solar cells.
method: Represent complex chemical systems with a descriptor for heterogeneous substructures.
Use a graph neural network to learn organic–inorganic inter-graph interactions.
Predict band gaps of hybrid solar cell materials.

infographic.watch_item: Generalization to new chemical families and improved solar-cell performance are not established by the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Learning Inter-Graph Interactions Between Heterogeneous Substructures of Chemical Systems

title: Coupling Evaporation, Chemical Reactions, and Crystallization: A Population-Balance Framework Applied to Two-Step Perovskite Crystallization
authors: K. Segadlo, O. J. J. Ronsin, J. Harting
abstract: A limited understanding of how evaporation couples to crystallization pathways hampers control over the formation of solution-processed perovskite photoactive layers. Identifying these mechanisms-and learning how to select and tune them-is essential for achieving the desired crystal morphology and, ultimately, improving solar-cell performance and stability. To investigate crystallization pathways in evaporating thin films, we develop a simple and general zero-dimensional population-balance model that couples evaporation, chemical reactions, and crystallization. We use the model to explore a range of parameters for a solvent-solute system that follows a two-step crystallization pathway: solvent evaporation first induces formation of a crystalline precursor, which subsequently recrystallizes into the final phase. The model predicts the evolution of the film composition during drying and provides quantitative LaMer curves. Based on these results, we introduce a vocabulary of "supply limitations" and "rate limitations" that enables the interpretation of crystallization kinetics in terms of the governing process conditions.

infographic.key_insight: A coupled population-balance model predicts how evaporation drives crystalline precursor formation and subsequent recrystallization into the final perovskite phase.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Distinguishing supply limitations from rate limitations could guide drying conditions to better control perovskite-film crystallization.
method: Couple evaporation, chemical reactions, and crystallization in a zero-dimensional population-balance model.
Explore parameters governing a two-step crystallization pathway.
Track film composition and generate quantitative LaMer curves.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports model-based parameter exploration and predicted drying trajectories, but does not describe experimental validation.
infographic.watch_item: The zero-dimensional formulation does not resolve spatial gradients that may affect crystallization in practical thin films.
infographic.paper_title: Coupling Evaporation, Chemical Reactions, and Crystallization: A Population-Balance Framework Applied to Two-Step Perovskite Crystallization

title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, Alan Zhan, Lamtiur P. Samosir, David S. Ginger*
abstract: Studying real-time degradation in perovskite semiconductors remains an important challenge. Conventional methods often cannot separate interfacial and bulk processes or rely on destructive analysis. Here, we demonstrate multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence (PL) as a nondestructive approach to distinguish interface- and bulk-dominated recombination losses. Using phenethylammonium tetrafluoroborate (PEABF4) treatment as a model, we use PL to show that PEABF4 passivates the electron transport layer (ETL)/perovskite interface, reducing interfacial recombination losses from fullerene deposition. However, upon thermal aging, PEABF4-treated stacks degrade more rapidly, with recombination losses broadening from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber. Diffusion-recombination simulations support interpreting excitation-wavelength-dependent PL decay signatures consistent with changes in surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime, providing a framework for depth-sensitive comparisons during aging. Collectively, these results further establish multiwavelength excitation PL as a platform for studying recombination losses during aging of perovskite films.

infographic.key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination but accelerates degradation under thermal aging, with losses extending into the perovskite bulk.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Nondestructive, depth-sensitive monitoring can help engineers distinguish initial interface-passivation benefits from long-term thermal-stability trade-offs in perovskite solar cells.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe interface- and bulk-dominated photoluminescence responses.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret decay signatures using diffusion–recombination simulations.
infographic.evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination losses from fullerene deposition after treatment, followed by faster thermal degradation; simulations support interpreting the wavelength-dependent signatures through surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime changes.
infographic.watch_item: Depth localization is model-supported rather than direct imaging, and the abstract provides no quantitative degradation rates or device-lifetime validation.
infographic.paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells

title: Magnetoelectric Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Solids
authors: Longjun Xiang, Fuming Xu, Lei Zhang, Jian Wang
abstract: It is commonly believed that a bulk photovoltaic current requires broken spatial inversion symmetry. However, in this work, we demonstrate that dc photocurrents can arise in centrosymmetric solids from the bilinear coupling between the electric and magnetic components of light. This magnetoelectric bulk photovoltaic effect (MBPE) has a quantum-geometric origin in the dipole moments of the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature. We identify four distinct MBPE mechanisms, including time-reversal-even and time-reversal-odd injection-like and shift-like photocurrents driven by linearly or circularly polarized light. Our symmetry analysis shows that the MBPE is allowed in broad classes of two-dimensional centrosymmetric nonmagnetic and magnetic materials under normally incident light. As representative examples, we predict sizable MBPEs in centrosymmetric monolayer Pt$_2$HgSe$_3$ and altermagnetic RuF$_4$, with current densities on the order of $1~\mathrm{mA/m}$. Notably, the injection-like photocurrent in RuF$_4$ reverses sign upon switching either the light helicity or the Néel vector. Our results extend the bulk photovoltaic effect to centrosymmetric solids and open new opportunities for electrical readout of altermagnetic order.

infographic.key_insight: Centrosymmetric solids can generate dc photocurrents through coupling between light’s electric and magnetic fields, without requiring broken inversion symmetry.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The magnetoelectric bulk photovoltaic effect expands candidate materials for photodetection and could enable electrical readout of altermagnetic order.
method: Connect photocurrents to dipole moments of the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature.
Classify four injection-like and shift-like mechanisms by polarization and time-reversal symmetry.
Predict responses in centrosymmetric monolayer Pt₂HgSe₃ and altermagnetic RuF₄.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract predicts current densities on the order of 1 mA/m and sign reversal of RuF₄’s injection-like photocurrent when either light helicity or the Néel vector is switched.
infographic.watch_item: The reported responses are predictions; experimental validation and practical solar-cell efficiency are not established in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Magnetoelectric Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Solids

title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
authors: Jelena Simeunović, Baptiste Schubnel, Pierre-Jean Alet, Pascal Frossard, Rafael E. Carrillo
abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph to capture the dynamics of these processes. We introduce a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PING) for forecasting future advection-diffusion particle concentrations on irregular grids. The model incorporates a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the loss function to guide learning toward physically consistent solutions. This model is on par with state of the art models on synthetic and real transport phenomena datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index datasets. Furthermore, the PING model is successfully coupled with models for forecasting PV power production. This hybrid approach leverages data fusion from ground-based sensors at PV stations and satellite images with cloud concentration to improve the accuracy of intra-day PV power production.

infographic.key_insight: PING uses a physics-informed graph neural network to forecast transport dynamics on irregular sensor networks and support improved solar power forecasting.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Better intra-day PV power forecasts can help grid operators integrate solar generation; this work targets forecasting rather than solar-cell device optimization.
method: Represent advection–diffusion particle concentrations as signals on a graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models that fuse ground-based sensor data and satellite cloud imagery.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting without numerical gains specified.
infographic.watch_item: A soft physics constraint guides learning but does not guarantee physical consistency.
infographic.paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting

title: How Memristors Work: A Step-by-Step Guide to the CALM Model
authors: Juan Bisquert
abstract: Memristors made of very different materials, halide perovskites, metal oxides and nanofluidic channels, show a common set of dynamical features: two limiting conductances, hysteresis that depends on the scan rate, regular and inverted hysteresis loops, large and negative capacitances and inductive loops in impedance spectra, and potentiation and depression under pulse trains. This tutorial shows how a single minimal model, the conductance-activated quasi-linear memristor (CALM) model, explains all these features with three ingredients: the two conductance states, the rectification function x_eq (u) and the characteristic time tau(u). The tutorial is a slide presentation that the reader can follow alone, with exercises designed to be solved with the help of an AI assistant, reference Python code, and this support text. The text can also be read on its own: Section 4 gives a compact account of the content of the slides, with the main equations and figures, and the solutions to the exercises are given at the end.

infographic.key_insight: The minimal CALM model explains diverse memristor dynamics using two conductance states, an equilibrium rectification function, and a voltage-dependent characteristic time.
infographic.engineering_relevance: CALM offers a compact framework for interpreting perovskite and other memristive devices, rather than a demonstrated AI method for improving solar-cell performance.
method: Represent switching between two limiting conductance states.
Describe state evolution through x_eq(u) and tau(u).
Explore responses with tutorial exercises and reference Python code.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract describes explanations of scan-rate-dependent hysteresis, capacitive and inductive impedance features, and pulse-driven potentiation and depression, but reports no quantitative validation metrics.
infographic.watch_item: Material-specific parameter calibration and predictive accuracy are not established in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: How Memristors Work: A Step-by-Step Guide to the CALM Model

title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou
abstract: Existing machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells struggle to predict devices made from new materials. Most treat device layers as arbitrary categorical labels and represent perovskite absorbers either through featureless composition vectors or through rigid crystal graphs that require a pre-solved unit cell. As a result, they cannot generalize to unrecorded alloys or unfamiliar cell architectures. We present the Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System (V-PaSS), an architecture built around the physical continuity of perovskite solid solutions. V-PaSS represents arbitrary mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure $ABX_3$ endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. For the device stack, it couples layer sequence and cell polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n) with interfacial band offsets and encodes chemical descriptions with a scientific language model. Evaluated under an institution-grouped protocol where test devices come exclusively from unseen laboratories, an untuned default configuration of V-PaSS achieves the lowest error among fourteen tested models (2.861% MAE, a 5.2% relative reduction over a gradient-boosted baseline at 3.017%, and outperforming the best tuned benchmark at 2.912%). V-PaSS pulls furthest ahead where test devices differ most from training: reducing error by 15.7-19.0% on unseen absorber alloys, by 16.1% on mixed absorbers from new laboratories, and widening its lead over the baseline by 3.6$\times$ on devices with unobserved transport layers. Combined with tree ensembles, V-PaSS sets a new state of the art across all five benchmark splits.

infographic.key_insight: V-PaSS uses physics-aware representations of perovskite alloys and device stacks to improve efficiency prediction for unfamiliar materials and architectures.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could help prioritize new absorber compositions and transport-layer combinations before fabricating solar cells.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs from 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, cell polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
infographic.evidence_signal: On institution-grouped testing with unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with 15.7–19.0% error reductions on unseen absorber alloys.
infographic.watch_item: Performance on unseen laboratory records does not establish prospective accuracy for newly fabricated devices or alloys that depart from the interpolation assumptions.
infographic.paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells

title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
authors: Jun Du, Liming Liu, Jun Yan
abstract: This work proposes an exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion (EKDD) model that bridges device-level charge transport with singlet and triplet excited-state kinetics. State populations and reversible photophysical transitions are solved self-consistently, enabling transient and steady-state device response calculations. We investigate how LE-CT, CT-CS, and LE-T energy offsets, together with triplet-transfer kinetics, govern charge generation, recombination, voltage loss, and extraction in organic photovoltaics. We identify CT-CS offset as a primary, largely overlooked factor controlling charge generation and voltage loss. A positive offset makes CT3-CS separation exothermic and improves generation, but lowers CS energy and increases voltage loss; a negative offset makes separation endothermic and highly temperature-sensitive. The model reproduces triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends. We propose design rules for balanced generation and voltage loss via two charge-transfer channels: the LE-CT-CS pathway favors a moderate LE-CT offset of about 0.15-0.20 eV and a weakly exothermic CT-CS offset of about 0.05-0.075 eV; the T-CT3-CS pathway requires the same CT-CS alignment plus a small CT-T offset, no more than about 0.1 eV, corresponding to a recycling factor K greater than about 10^-2, to maintain fast T-to-CT3 recycling. CT-CS alignment is the main determinant of the charge-generation-voltage-loss trade-off, while triplet-recycling kinetics determines whether this balance survives at the device level. This work provides a unified theoretical description from exciton generation to free charge collection, offering a convenient tool for transient and steady-state analysis in organic photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Organic photovoltaic performance depends primarily on CT–CS energy alignment, while fast triplet recycling helps preserve the balance between charge generation and voltage loss.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The model suggests targeting LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV.
method: Couple singlet and triplet exciton kinetics with drift–diffusion charge transport.
Solve state populations and reversible transitions self-consistently.
Evaluate transient and steady-state responses across energy offsets and triplet-transfer rates.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, but provides no quantitative validation metrics.
infographic.watch_item: This is a physics-based device model, not an AI method; the proposed design windows require broader experimental validation.
infographic.paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics

title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
authors: Kirill Sobolev, Nagaprasad Reddy Samala, Mariela J. Pavan, Sharon Hazan, Vladimir Ezersky, Shakked Schwartz
abstract: The integration of two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXenes into Halide Perovskite (HaP) optoelectronics has shown immense potential for enhancing device performance, yet the fundamental chemical interactions within the precursor ink (a critical stage determining the final material state) remain largely unexplored. This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the chemical stability and surface evolution of Ti3C2Tx MXenes when exposed to the individual and combined components of a model methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) solution. By combining detailed X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) analysis with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, we decouple the complex interactions between MXenes and the ink constituents. We demonstrate that elemental iodine (I2) and polyiodides (In-) act as aggressive oxidizers, triggering rapid degradation and dissolution of the MXene flakes. Conversely, lead iodide (PbI2) induces a slower oxidation process driven by the strong adsorption of Pb2+ ions onto oxygen terminated sites. In stark contrast, methylammonium iodide (MAI) exhibits a stabilizing effect: it adsorbs onto the MXene surface via hydrogen bonding, effectively passivating the flakes and retarding degradation. In addition, our results reveal that the sequence of precursor addition governs the MXene surface state, requiring extra caution, but also enabling further tunability. These findings provide a critical view on how MXene integration with materials, in general, and HaP in particular, should be perceived, providing a fundamental for their rational engineering.

infographic.key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the chemical species present and their addition sequence: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide provides surface passivation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor chemistry and mixing order could help preserve MXenes during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track surface chemistry.
Apply density functional theory to investigate adsorption interactions.
infographic.evidence_signal: Combined XPS analysis and DFT calculations support rapid degradation by iodine and polyiodides, slower PbI2-induced oxidation, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization by MAI.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports model-ink chemistry, not quantified device-performance gains or long-term solar-cell stability.
infographic.paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments

title: Multi-property Feynman-Kac Steering of Crystal Diffusion Models
authors: Oded Mousai, Sapir Esther Yiflach, Barak Itzchak Davidovitch, Yuval Mualem, Sarit Kraus, Hannah-Noa Barad
abstract: Pretrained diffusion models provide powerful priors for generating new materials, including inorganic crystals, but generating useful materials requires satisfying specific chemical and physical properties, from mechanical stiffness to bandgaps. Existing approaches either retrain models for new target properties or steer only the atom coordinates and lattice during generation, leaving composition unchanged despite its fundamental role in determining physical properties. We present FK-ReMask, an inference-time, gradient-free method that steers both the continuous and discrete channels of a pretrained crystal diffusion model. During generation, FK-ReMask maintains multiple denoising trajectories and replicates promising candidates using Feynman-Kac particle selection. However, selection alone is insufficient: in the atom-type channel, committed elements cannot be revised, so cloning propagates existing compositions and limits the population's ability to explore new ones. We address this with an atom re-masking mechanism, which reopens committed sites during the generation process and allows alternative compositions to emerge. Across four electronic, photovoltaic, and mechanical objectives, our method improves the yield of SUN (stable, unique, novel) and property-on-target materials. We further demonstrate joint steering of three photovoltaic properties, showing that multiple physical objectives can be specified entirely at inference time without retraining.

infographic.key_insight: FK-ReMask steers a pretrained crystal diffusion model toward desired material properties by revising both crystal geometry and elemental composition without retraining.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For photovoltaic materials discovery, it enables joint targeting of three physical properties at inference time rather than requiring a newly trained model for each objective.
method: Maintain multiple denoising trajectories and replicate promising candidates using Feynman–Kac particle selection.
Re-mask committed atom types so candidates can explore alternative elemental compositions.
Apply gradient-free steering across continuous and discrete generation channels.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across four electronic, photovoltaic, and mechanical objectives, the abstract reports improved yield of stable, unique, novel and property-on-target materials, plus joint steering of three photovoltaic properties.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not quantify gains or computational overhead, and generated candidates do not establish experimentally validated solar-cell performance.
infographic.paper_title: Multi-property Feynman-Kac Steering of Crystal Diffusion Models

title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
authors: Michael Seifert, Miguel A. L. Marques, Silvana Botti
abstract: P-type transparent conducting materials (TCMs) remain scarce, limiting progress in transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics. Here, we perform a high-throughput computational search across CuI-based ternary X--Cu--I compounds using the minima hopping method combined with density functional theory. Filtering for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass, we identify 58 candidate p-type TCMs, of which 49 are previously unreported. Twenty are p-type degenerate semiconductors with intrinsic hole carriers, including Cu$_2$FI$_2$ (calculated gap 3.75 eV, hole effective mass $0.262\,m_0$). We further use this dataset to revisit the chemical modulation of the valence band (CMVB) design rules, originally formulated for Cu-based delafossite oxides. Four generalizations emerge: linear Cu coordination is not required, as tetrahedral coordination (CN = 4) is compatible with p-type TCM character; the mechanism extends to halide-based systems with I $5p$ anion states; the Cu $d$ state energy center $ε_d$ is a quantitative descriptor for valence band dispersion; and Cu undercoordination in monovalent-anion hosts drives intrinsic p-type carrier generation through stoichiometric charge balance. These results establish a generalized computational framework for the design of p-type halide TCMs.

infographic.key_insight: A computational search identified 58 candidate CuI-based ternary p-type transparent conductors and generalized design rules beyond oxide systems.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These materials could expand transparent hole-conducting options for tandem photovoltaics and transparent electronics, although solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Search X–Cu–I structures using minima hopping and density functional theory.
Filter for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Analyze Cu coordination and electronic states to generalize valence-band design rules.
infographic.evidence_signal: Of 58 computational candidates, 49 were previously unreported and 20 were intrinsically p-type degenerate semiconductors; Cu₂FI₂ had a calculated 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m₀ hole effective mass.
infographic.watch_item: Experimental synthesis, transparency, conductivity, and device compatibility remain to be validated.
infographic.paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors

title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
authors: Robert L. Z. Hoye, Markus Hellenbrand, Nuno Estrócio, Austin M. Kay, Alice Scardina, Alessandro Mezzetti
abstract: The exponential, pervasive rise of artificial intelligence (AI), hosted in large data centres, will test the limits of the underpinning infrastructure, including electricity and water supplies, which are becoming increasingly precious resources. Rather than performing all AI computations in centralized servers, for many functionalities, these can be performed locally across a network of billions of small, autonomous nodes, saving substantial energy costs associated with communication. This alternative paradigm is known as edge computing, or distributed intelligence (DI), but has been held back by the lack of availability of reliable local energy supplies matching the energy requirements of the computational infrastructure. Opportunities to address this challenge are emerging with rapid advances in high-performance indoor photovoltaics (IPVs) for local energy harvesting, as well as reductions in computational cost through neuromorphic or in-memory computing devices. In this perspective, we discuss the requirements of IPVs for DI, the extent to which emerging materials fulfil these requirements, and how current gaps could be addressed. We make the case that (anti)ferroelectric materials can surpass bottlenecks for both electrostatic energy storage and low-power in-memory neuromorphic computing. The core theme of this perspective is that co-creation between energy harvesting, storage and computing is essential for making DI a reliable and more sustainable alternative to centralized AI.

infographic.key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics paired with (anti)ferroelectric energy storage and low-power computing could enable autonomous edge AI nodes that reduce reliance on centralized data centres.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reliable distributed intelligence requires co-designing indoor energy harvesting, storage and computation to match local power availability with device demand.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence.
Discuss how emerging photovoltaic materials meet these requirements and address remaining gaps.
Examine (anti)ferroelectrics for electrostatic storage and low-power in-memory neuromorphic computing.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract presents a perspective on emerging technologies, not a demonstrated integrated system or quantified performance evaluation.
infographic.watch_item: Reliable operation remains contingent on matching variable indoor energy supply with storage capacity and computational workloads.
infographic.paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
